I added the missing `break` statements to the `number`, `dateTime`, `boolean`, `array` and `object` cases in `executeFilterCondition`. Tests and typecheck pass, but lint couldn't run, and I didn't confirm that the new test fails without the fix.

Those cases ended without a `break`. An operation that didn't match any inner case therefore fell through into the next type's switch. For example, a `number` condition with operation `true` ran the `boolean` branch and returned `left`. Now it reaches the existing "Unknown filter parameter operator" warning and returns `false`. The change is in `src/node-parameters/filter-parameter.ts`.

I added a regression test in `test/filter-parameter.test.ts` for `number` with `true`, `boolean` with `lengthGt`, and `dateTime` with `true`. I left out an `array` case because it only falls through into `object`, which also ends in the warning, so there is no visible difference.

## fix(core): Add missing break statements in filter condition evaluation

Added missing `break` statements after the inner operation switches for number, dateTime, boolean, array and object cases in executeFilterCondition, so unsupported operations no longer fall through into the next type's switch and now reach the 'Unknown filter parameter operator' warning and return false. Added regression tests for cross-type fallthrough.

### What changed
- 1 source file(s), 1 test file(s), 34 changed lines
- `packages/workflow/src/node-parameters/filter-parameter.ts`

### What ran
- The agent ran the tests 2 time(s) and says: acdc-test test/filter-parameter.test.ts: 225 passed. acdc-typecheck printed nothing, which I take as a pass. acdc-lint did not run: 'Failed to find tsgolint executable'. I did not run the new tests against the unfixed code to confirm they fail there.
- Type check: passes; lint: not available for this commit
- Tests for the issue: 1/1; tests that passed before: 235/235

### Risks that remain
- Change risk: medium (10% chance of a revert or follow-up fix, from n8n's history)
- Lint could not be run in this environment, so formatting and lint of the edits are unchecked.
- The new tests cast an invalid type/operation pair to force the unsupported case. Number-to-boolean and boolean-to-array are the observable fallthroughs; dateTime-to-boolean is included as well.
- The new tests use typeValidation 'loose', which I chose to avoid strict conversion errors; check that this matches what you intend to cover.
- Behaviour changes only for invalid operator/type combinations, which previously could return arbitrary results.
